newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nomura's share of TSE stock trading drops.
newsitem.headline: Nomura's share of TSE stock trading drops.

text.p: Scandal-hit Nomura Securities Co Ltd said on Thursday that its stock transactions accounted for 6.0 percent of the total value of transactions on the Tokyo Stock Exchange in the April-to-June quarter, down from 11.3 percent in the year-ago period.

Nomura said in a statement that its stock broking commissions dropped by 37.6 percent year-on-year to 22.9 billion yen in the April-to-June quarter, while bond trading commissions slid by 41.6 percent to 3.7 billion yen.

Nomura and two other major brokerages, Daiwa Securities Co Ltd and Nikko Securities Co Ltd, unveiled their quarterly earnings on Thursday. Yamaichi Securities Co Ltd, the other "Big Four" brokerage, will announce its quarterly earnings on Friday.

Daiwa said that its stock transactions in the quarter accounted for 9.6 percent of the total trading value on the Tokyo bourse, up from 9.1 percent a year ago. Nikko reported that its share in the quarter fell to 8.2 percent from 8.7 percent in the same period a year earlier.

Nomura's commissions from stock and bond underwriting and secondary offerings took a steep 78.7 percent dive to 3.46 billion yen from the same quarter a year ago. Overall commissions on bond, stock and other transactions slid 36.9 percent to 53.63 billion yen.

Nomura was hit hard by a racketeer payoff scandal, which prompted Japan's securities watchdog to urge the finance minister to impose penalties against Nomura. The scandal has already cast a long shadow over the brokerage's business and prompted many clients to shun the financial powerhouse.

The penalties, if adopted, would be the heaviest ever imposed by the ministry. Tokyo prosecutors have indicted Nomura itself, its former president Hideo Sakamaki and former managing director Nobutaka Fujikura on charges of making illegal payoffs to a "sokaiya" corporate racketeer.
